title: Grier
summary: Grier, born Prince Zan-Grier of Sutos Island, served as DeFoe’s right-hand man. Rarely speaking, he presented himself an ordinary thug, but he carries himself with a subtle nobility with his loyalty. sections.heading: History
sections.text:
, dies in his arms]]
Though few were aware, Grier was raised on the secret Seeker island-nation of Sutos, where his father, Zan-Sutos, ruled as leader. His family had led the people of this nation to an orderly, happy existence for many years. After his father's death, Grier moved on to the Organization to do his part to bring order to the world using his Seeker skills. With many battles and defeats at the hands of Dante's team, DeFoe lost the favor of the Organization and Grier was chosen to replace him only after he got rid of DeFoe. Grier soon returns to his home and restores order to the island torn apart by war, thereafter being recognized as the new ruler. [Like Father, Unlike Son]

After the defeat of the Professor, Dante Vale and his team returned to Sutos Island to ask for help from Grier. His men were attacked by the Blood Spiral Brotherhood. Grier guided the team through the Professor's castle in order to find the dossier about Rassimov. Grier later helped Lok Lambert and Den Fears defeat Mr. Wilder in the Professor's room. As a result of this, he captured Mr. Wilder and took over the Organization. [An Ally from the Organization]

sections.heading: Personality
sections.wikitext:
[[File:S1E12 Grier 1.png|190px|thumb]]
At first glance, Grier comes off as a robotic yes-man, just another arm of his commander DeFoe, but under his seemingly blind loyalty is a much more complex, likable man. He is an idealist as well as a loyalist, always committed to bringing order to a chaotic world. Behind his strong loyalty beats a heart of honor that desires to bring peace to [[Sutos Island]]. {{Source|S1E12}} In many ways Grier could be considered the ideal ruler as he prioritized the needs and safety of his people over going to fight an unknown war. {{Source|S2E46}} Grier was extremely pragmatic in making decisions, as he was conflicted about killing [[DeFoe]], but ultimately decided to do it as it was in the best interests of his goal to return to Sutos and bring peace to his homeland. {{Source|S1E11}}

sections.heading: Dante Vale
sections.wikitext:
[[File:S1E03 Grier restrains Dante.png|190px|thumb|Grier restrains [[Dante Vale|Dante]] during one of their numerous clashes]]
Grier had an intense rivalry with [[Dante Vale]], as both were powerful and charismatic Seekers harboring strong values. The more the two fought, the more they recognized that the other was fighting for the good of mankind, though both had very different ideas of this good. Extremely well-matched in physical combat, their conflicts were often resolved between their two gargantuan [[Titans]]: Dante's [[Metagolem]] and Grier's signature Titan, the bear-brawler, [[Breaker]], with this fighting rivalry reaching its peak when the two men battled it out on [[Sutos Island]]. Grier himself stated that he had waited his whole life to fight an opponent like Dante {{Source|Like Father, Unlike Son}} and Lok described their relationship to [[Den Fears]] as having been that of archenemies. {{source|An Ally from the Organization}}

sections.heading: DeFoe
sections.wikitext:
[[File:S1E11 Grier kills DeFoe.png|thumb|190px|Grier kills [[DeFoe]]]]
Extremely respectful of his superiors, Grier was initially loyal and respectful to [[DeFoe]] as his right-hand man and followed his orders obediently. {{Source|S1E03}} However, over time, as DeFoe's plans continued to fail, this relationship grew increasingly strained. Grier began to grow more weary of DeFoe's antics, notably his cowardice in leaving his men behind in the [[Cave of the Gargoyle]] {{Source|Crawling the Catacombs}}, and his continued poor judgement and tendency to prioritize his hate-fuelled vendetta against Dante Vale over the missions of the Organization. {{Source|Divide and Conquer}} He challenged DeFoe when he violated delivering the [[Sword of Saint George]] and eventually took control of the situation on [[Atalanta's Ship]], carrying an insane DeFoe back to [[Organization Central]] and leaving him to be punished by [[Rassimov]]. {{Source|The Treasures of the Argonauts}} When [[the Professor]] chose Grier to replace DeFoe, but on the condition that he "disposed" of him first, Grier was initially conflicted but he ultimately determined that DeFoe was a chaotic individual who would not follow orders. In order to carry out his ambitions of returning to his homeland, Grier killed him. {{source|The Beautiful Trap}} Grier was not proud of killing DeFoe, and hinted that this was part of the reason that he felt he should remain on [[Sutos]] when Dante asked him to join the [[Huntik Foundation]]. {{Source|S2E46}}

sections.heading: Abilities
sections.wikitext:
[[File:S2E46_Grier_invokes_Breaker.png|thumb|Grier invokes [[Breaker]]]]
Grier is a powerful [[Seeker]], able to fight on equal ground with [[Dante Vale]]. For many of his missions, Grier never fought at full power, and none of his superiors were aware just how strong a Seeker he was. When fighting him on [[Sutos]], Dante stated that he was at least twice as fast as he was before. {{Source|S1E12}} In combat, Grier uses his raw strength to deliver knockout punches, while using magic that makes him faster and much stronger than any normal human such as [[Shadowspeed]] or [[Dragonfist]]. With him fights [[Breaker]], a mighty Titan that hits hard with a combination of strength and speed, and can even take down the mighty [[Caliban]] singehandedly. {{Source|S1E09}}

sections.heading: Bonded Titans
sections.text:
Breaker, Powerbonded — TV Series — Grier's Signature bear-brawler; he became Powerbonded to save Grier from suffocation at the hands of Grand Façade.

Megataur — TV Series — The royal fighting Titan of Sutos, it once belonged to Grier's father, Zan-Sutos; after his death, the Governor kept it safe until Grier's return.

Mindrone — TV Series — The go-to Organization Titan for scouting, Grier used his Mindrone when fighting Dante on Sutos.

Redcap — TV Series — The most common Organization Titan, Grier summoned his Redcap to back up Breaker in the Paris Catacombs.

Unnamed Titan 010 — TCG — A towering abundance of monoliths covered in Egyptian hieroglyphics used by Grier to clear large areas.
